subject: sociology
title: Power and Authority
welcome_lead: Why do we obey teachers, monarchs and managers? Start with Weber's three classic forms of authority.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on Weber's three types of authority and the difference between power and authority.
final_note: You can now tell coercion from authority and name Weber's three legitimate forms.

concepts.def: The ability to make others do what you want.
Power that people accept as legitimate.
Weber: power from a leader's personal appeal.
Weber: power from laws and offices.
Power based on threat or use of force.

walkthroughs.body_html: A robber forces you with a gun: that is coercion. A teacher tells you to sit down and you obey: that is authority. Weber said authority works because people see it as legitimate.
Traditional: 'we have always done it this way' (monarchy). Charismatic: people follow a personality (Gandhi, Martin Luther King). Legal-rational: rules and offices (judges, MPs, head teachers).
Most modern leaders blend types. A monarch (traditional) acts within parliament (legal-rational). A US president needs charisma to win but governs under the constitution (legal-rational).
